subject: lavaan ERROR: at least one variance in the sample covariance matrix is not finite.

messages.author: 693670b12cd395ae
messages.subject: lavaan ERROR: at least one variance in the sample covariance matrix is not finite.
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to estimate a sem model using very simple syntax. The model is only a regression with interaction terms as:

model = "y ~ x1 +  x1:x2 + x3 + x3:x2 + x2 + x4 + x5" 

Using this syntax, the model works:

est <- sem(model = model, data = dataset , estimator = "ML")

However, using a covariance matrix created out of the very same dataset and using this covariance matrix as input, like this:

est<- sem(model = model, sample.cov = covariance, sample.nobs = 3200, estimator = "ML")

I get the following error and warnings

Error in lavData(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster, ov.names = OV.NAMES,  : 
                   lavaan ERROR: at least one variance in the sample covariance matrix is not finite.
                 : Warning message:
                   In diag(sample.cov[[g]]) : NAs introduced by coercion

Why could this happen? What does "at least one variance in the sample covariance matrix is not finite" means? Does anybody know why this error may arise?

Thank you very much!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: lavaan ERROR: at least one variance in the sample covariance matrix is not finite.
parts: However, using a covariance matrix created out of the very same dataset

Are you sure?  Did you calculate the product terms in your model and include those variables in the covariance matrix?  In that case, you would need to use those variable names in your syntax, rather than using the colon operator to tell lavaan to calculate the product for you.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
